p2_concerns.issue: Partial RSS success advances the wrong recovery watermark
p2_concerns.code_flow: Live API begin uses state.last_success_at minus1day. poll_source writes last_success_at=now even when API fails and RSS succeeds, resulting in statuspartial. Repeated partial polls move that watermark past the original missing API interval.
p2_concerns.effect: After an API outage lasting multiple days, recovery scans only the most recent day and may never complete older missed API bodies/pages or corrections. A partial label preserves visibility but does not repair the missing interval.
p2_concerns.minimal_design: Keep a separate complete API success/recovery watermark that advances only after a complete primary API scan. RSS partial successes must not move it. Preserve sourcepartial while fallback data remains available.

p2_concerns.issue: Published-at-only primary scan plus unconditional known-API carry can miss real older-article revisions
p2_concerns.code_flow: Primary API query filters publishedAt since the recent begin. If a known API article is older than that range and its RSS metadata/body changes, _preserve_publisher_authority returns the oldrecord without validating the publisher API again.
p2_concerns.effect: Preventing a transport downgrade can also suppress a genuine source correction or ongoing-event update.
p2_concerns.minimal_design: Confirm changed known-API RSS observations through a single authoritative API record lookup, or use a verified updatedAt increment in addition to bounded publication discovery. Do not blindly accept lower-fidelity text as a revision.
